attrs.evidence: docs/spec/proof-wire/experiment/run_state.mjs IMPLEMENTATION_RE + observationFile(), which returns null rather than a path when the destination would escape; governance/blind_run.mjs refuses the label at --freeze-candidate and refuses to archive to a null destination. Falsifier X: `--implementation ../../../escape` is REFUSED and the run gains no adapter. Gate `gov-nest`; grid boolean conformance-replayed, whose label half is measured in both directions.
attrs.statement: AN IMPLEMENTATION LABEL IS AN IDENTIFIER, NOT A PATH. P4.7.3 made subjects unable to leave their world, and P4.7.4 then named each subject's archived observation document after its label while checking labels for uniqueness alone. REPRODUCED through the ordinary interface: `--freeze-candidate --implementation ../../../escape` was ACCEPTED and printed CANDIDATE_FROZEN, and the archive destination derived from that label resolves outside the observation directory -- one further `..` leaves governance/ altogether. The system that had just stopped a SUBJECT escaping its world let a subject's NAME carry its own terminal EVIDENCE out: the containment species one layer later, and the fourth time in this plane that a rule was enforced on one representation of a thing and not on another. Labels must match a boring identifier pattern, and INDEPENDENTLY the derived archive destination must resolve strictly beneath the observation directory -- positive containment verified rather than inferred from a pattern having matched, because two checks that can disagree are worth more than one that cannot be wrong. The rule is enforced at the freeze interface AND inside verifyRun, so a hand-edited record is caught by the same rule that refuses the command line.
